title: Equipment manufacturers
description: Design and manufacture transformers, switchgear, turbines, inverters, cables, and other grid hardware. Utilities and generators purchase the equipment.

title: Regulators
description: FERC oversees most interstate transmission tariffs and organized wholesale-market rules. State commissions typically oversee retail distribution rates and retail-supplier rules. Funding: FERC uses industry charges and filing fees; state commissions often use utility assessments. State arrangements vary.

title: ISOs / RTOs
description: Coordinate regional transmission operations, issue dispatch instructions to generators, plan system reliability, and administer organized wholesale markets. They generally do not own or maintain transmission lines.

title: Power plant operators
description: Build, own, operate and maintain generating assets. Sell power through wholesale markets or bilateral contracts; some also receive capacity or ancillary-service revenue.

title: Transmission utilities
description: Build, own, operate and maintain high-voltage lines and substations. Recover allowed costs and returns through FERC-regulated transmission tariffs charged to transmission customers.

title: Distribution utilities
description: Own and maintain local lines, distribution substations, meters and transformers. Recover approved distribution costs through regulated delivery charges on customers’ bills.

title: Retail electricity suppliers
description: Contract with end customers for electricity supply. Buy or hedge wholesale power and charge retail customers for the supply component of their bills. In many regions this is the distribution utility itself.

title: Generation facilities
description: Physical equipment converts primary energy into electrical power and injects that power into the network.

title: Transmission network
description: High-voltage conductors, breakers, transformers, protection systems and substations move bulk electrical energy across regions.

title: Distribution network
description: Medium- and low-voltage equipment delivers electrical power from substations to customers and isolates local faults.

title: Consumers
description: Consume delivered electricity and ultimately fund generation, grid infrastructure, and system services through electricity bills. Large industrial customers may connect directly to transmission.

title: Wholesale market & settlements
description: An ISO/RTO matches and settles wholesale energy transactions and administers transmission-related billing and credits. The financial flow shown is schematic; not every trade passes through a spot market.
